title: Cycle Alarm

story.briefing: A loop in the routing fabric sends packets round forever. Before the Core will accept this layout it wants to know whether any loop exists at all.
story.success: Fabric cleared. No packet can circle indefinitely.

description: A graph is given as n, the number of nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and edges, an array of [u, v] pairs. Edges are undirected unless stated otherwise, and there are no self-loops or duplicate edges. Return true if the graph contains a cycle — a path that leaves a node and returns to it without reusing any edge — and false otherwise.
hints: While walking the graph, reaching a node you have already visited is suspicious — but not proof, because the edge you just came along leads straight back to where you were.
You have to ignore the edge you arrived on, and only that one. Remember which node you came from at each step.

Walk each unvisited component, carrying the node you came from. If you meet a visited node that is not the one you came from, there is a cycle. Track the parent per node, and use an explicit stack rather than recursion.
